svg.title: Project 1 architecture: ismailoyeleke.com on AWS
svg.desc: Visitors resolve the domain in Route 53 and reach a CloudFront distribution protected by AWS WAF, with an ACM certificate and a CloudFront Function. CloudFront reads from a private S3 bucket in us-east-1 through Origin Access Control. Deploys run in GitHub Actions, which assume an IAM role through OIDC, sync the build to S3 and invalidate the CloudFront cache.

text.tspan: A static site with no servers: S3 for the files, CloudFront for HTTPS and caching, Route 53 for the domain, deployed from GitHub Actions through OIDC.
A + AAAA alias, apex and www
The browser asks Route 53 for ismailoyeleke.com and gets the CloudFront alias.
It connects to the nearest CloudFront edge over HTTPS. WAF filters the request first.
On a cache miss, CloudFront fetches the file from the private bucket, signed with OAC.
A push to main starts GitHub Actions, which swaps its OIDC token for short-lived AWS keys.
The built site is synced to the S3 bucket. No long-lived keys are stored anywhere.
The CloudFront cache is invalidated, so visitors get the new version straight away.
